title: ENGINE MOUNT - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What are the proper procedures and precautions for installing shock mounts to ensure noise reduction, proper alignment, and secure attachment to the engine and firewall?
answer: Shock Mount Procedures . (1) The shock mounts that connect the engine to the engine mount are made of a synthetic material and metal, which are installed to decrease noise and vibration. CAUTION: Do not clean the shock mounts with any type of solvent. (2) Use a clean, dry cloth to clean the shock mounts. (3) Examine the shock mounts and replace them as necessary. (a) Examine the metal parts for cracks and deterioration as a result of wear and age. (b) Examine the synthetic material for separation, swelling, cracks on the pad, and incorrect alignment with the engine. (4) When you install the shock mounts, make sure that you install them in the order that follows. (a) For the top shock mount, install the largest shock mount aft of the mounting flange. NOTE:  You can put zero, one, or two washers  between the tubular engine mount and each lower engine shock mount to correctly align the engine with the nose cap. (5) Make sure that the nuts are torqued to between 450 and 500 inch-pounds  for installation with no engine weight on the shock mounts.Firewall Mounting Procedures . (1) Attach the engine mount to the firewall with bolts, washers, flat washers, and nuts as illustrated in Figure 202. Torque the nuts to between 160 and 190 inch-pounds  with no engine weight on the shock mounts.Removal Notes. (1)  For specific engine mount removal instructions, refer to the Engine - Maintenance Practices section of this chapter.

title: ENGINE MOUNT - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What are the key considerations for inspecting the synthetic and metal components of shock mounts for wear and damage?
answer: Shock Mount Procedures . (1) The shock mounts that connect the engine to the engine mount are made of a synthetic material and metal, which are installed to decrease noise and vibration. CAUTION: Do not clean the shock mounts with any type of solvent. (2) Use a clean, dry cloth to clean the shock mounts. (3) Examine the shock mounts and replace them as necessary. (a) Examine the metal parts for cracks and deterioration as a result of wear and age. (b) Examine the synthetic material for separation, swelling, cracks on the pad, and incorrect alignment with the engine. (4) When you install the shock mounts, make sure that you install them in the order that follows. (a) For the top shock mount, install the largest shock mount aft of the mounting flange. NOTE:  You can put zero, one, or two washers  between the tubular engine mount and each lower engine shock mount to correctly align the engine with the nose cap. (5) Make sure that the nuts are torqued to between 450 and 500 inch-pounds  for installation with no engine weight on the shock mounts.Firewall Mounting Procedures . (1) Attach the engine mount to the firewall with bolts, washers, flat washers, and nuts as illustrated in Figure 202. Torque the nuts to between 160 and 190 inch-pounds  with no engine weight on the shock mounts.Removal Notes. (1)  For specific engine mount removal instructions, refer to the Engine - Maintenance Practices section of this chapter.
